summary: Use Brand Chip to identify a linked brand or account with an avatar and a short label.

useWhen.text: Identify a linked brand or account with an avatar and a short label.

from.quote: Use Brand Chip to identify a linked brand or account with an avatar and a short label.

useWhen.text: Show the account in use, such as the account a payment is made from (the guide's “Paying from”).

from.quote: Show the account in use

avoidWhen.text: Showing a status such as Payment complete: a status label no longer tells people which account is involved. Put the status in nearby content and keep the chip for the account.

from.quote: A status label no longer tells people which account is involved.

anatomy.holds: The brand's image (imageSource) or the Avatar given in avatarSlot, such as a monogram; helps recognize the brand.

from.quote: Helps recognize the brand.

anatomy.holds: label: names the account and distinguishes it from similar accounts.

from.quote: Names the account and distinguishes it from similar accounts.

placementAdvice.text: Let the surrounding composition explain the chip's role, such as a “Paying from” line above it.

from.quote: The surrounding composition explains the chip’s role.

placementAdvice.text: The chip grows with its content: it hugs its avatar and label rather than filling its host.

from.quote: The chip grows with its content.

placementAdvice.text: The label is one line by default; in constrained hosts, use short identifiers.

from.quote: Its label is one line by default; use short identifiers in constrained hosts.

configuration.text: Keep the avatar and the label about the same brand.

from.quote: Keep the avatar and label about the same brand.

configuration.text: Use an avatar or monogram for the brand named in the label.

from.quote: Use an avatar or monogram for the brand named in the label.

configuration.text: Do not pair the label with another brand's avatar or monogram (such as HB beside Axis Bank • 0245): a different brand cue creates uncertainty about the account.

from.quote: A different brand cue creates uncertainty about the account.

configuration.text: When no brand image is available, a monogram gives a clear fallback: an Avatar with style Monogram in avatarSlot, such as AB for Axis Bank.

from.quote: A monogram can provide a clear fallback when an image is unavailable.

configuration.text: The monogram is supplied through avatarSlot by the screen: BrandChip does not replace a failed image with a monogram on its own.

from.quote: The monogram here is supplied through the public avatarSlot; it is not an automatic image-error fallback.

configuration.text: imageSource puts the brand's image in the chip's own Avatar; it is ignored when avatarSlot is given.
BrandChip already shows its avatar at Avatar Size S (29 px, as in Figma) and passes its modes on to the Avatar in avatarSlot.

from.quote: Brand Chip forwards its modes recursively and defaults the slot Avatar to S

configuration.text: Make the chip actionable (onPress) only when pressing it opens account detail or a choice; to identify the current account, leave it static.

from.quote: Make it actionable only when it opens account detail or a choice.

rules.text: Pair a recognizable identity with just enough text to distinguish it.

from.quote: Pair a recognizable identity with just enough text to distinguish it.
Keep the brand name recognizable.

rules.text: Include the account suffix when more than one account shares the same brand, such as Axis Bank • 0245 and Axis Bank • 1182.

from.quote: Include the account suffix when more than one account shares the same brand.

rules.text: Do not give different accounts identical labels.

from.quote: Avoid identical labels for different accounts.

rules.text: Prefer a short brand name and a distinguishing account suffix.

from.quote: Prefer a short brand name and a distinguishing account suffix.

rules.text: Keep the identifier compact: the brand and the distinguishing suffix.

from.quote: Keep the brand and the distinguishing suffix.

rules.text: Do not write a full description (such as Axis Bank savings account • 0245): long descriptions consume space needed by surrounding content.

from.quote: Long descriptions consume space needed by surrounding content.

rules.text: Put a transaction status in nearby content, not in the label.

from.quote: Use nearby content for the transaction status.

states.when: Without onPress: a read-only chip that identifies the current account.

from.quote: Use a static chip to identify the current account.

states.when: With onPress the chip can be pressed. Use it when pressing opens account detail or a choice, and not otherwise.

from.quote: Make it actionable only when it opens account detail or a choice.

accessibility.text: The chip's accessibility label defaults to its label; set accessibilityLabel to replace it.

<Card variant="slim">

    <Text>Paying from</Text>

    />
  </VStack>
</Card>

props.name: label
props.description: One line by default, and the label lacks flex shrink: the chip hugs its content, so a long label is not promised to fit a narrow host (the guide's long-label example runs past its 240 px host). Declared: Visible label (e.g. `"Axis Bank • 0245"`). Default "Axis Bank • 0245", from the component source.

props.name: imageSource
props.description: Image shown in the avatar. Forwarded to the underlying `Avatar`'s `imageSource` prop. Pass a `require()`-ed asset, an `{ uri }` object or a remote URL string. Ignored when `avatarSlot` is provided.

props.name: avatarSlot
props.description: Gets the chip's modes recursively and Avatar Size S by default. BrandChip does not replace a failed image with a monogram: a monogram is an Avatar the screen puts in the slot. Declared: Slot replacing the default `Avatar`. Receives `modes` recursively, so inner `Avatar` / `IconCapsule` instances inherit theming.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Optional press handler — when provided, the chip becomes a `Pressable`.

props.name: modes
props.description: Design token modes for theming (e.g. `{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }`).

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, disables text truncation: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and any `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored, so the text wraps to as many lines as it needs even when horizontal space is tight.

modes.name: Avatar Size
modes.description: BrandChip shows its avatar at S (29 px, Figma's size) unless its modes set Avatar Size. Declared: A token collection BrandChip reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

gaps.text: BrandChip has no selected or disabled state: the package offers an optional action (onPress) only.
The label has no flex shrink, so a long label can run past a narrow host: the guide’s long-label example exceeds its 240 px host. Keep identifiers short.
